It took me a while to actually start liking this game. It is both completely nonsensical and at the same time emotionally poignant. It's hard for me to fully express how I feel about this game. The combat isn't great even by rpg standards. But there's enough interesting stuff to do that I don't mind for the most part. Yeah I don't know what to say about it, but I'm glad I played it.

Enjoy the whip-lash educing experience as you jump frantically from serious and dark mafia style drama; (pretty well written too!) to a segment where you fend off hoards of suit wearing sheep in order to watch a movie with a bro.

Humble Bundled!

Almost your standard Yakuza game, so if you like yakuza games, you're probably good to go.

There's a few curveballs to the formula, combat is RPG style which introduces a few peccadilloes, and a lot of the minigames are all still very present but weirdly don't have much impact at all, which i found nice because I didn't want to do most of them. 

The three worst things were (least to most) hunting for cockroaches to upgrade stuff, the elevator commands in the sotenburi arena, and the very worst part of the game was the management job. 

Compared to zero/kiwami manager jobs, now your job is... absolute tedium. Now you must: hold right trigger, press x 50 times to get through daily summary. repeat 3x. match colors for stockholders. Oops! Don't forget after every day to go to employee screen, press x, accept cost to "heal" your employees willingness to work. repeat x 432047320329743209 however long you're willing to suffer to generate cash to upgrade your weapons.

By the time I was done, I'd definitely done too much grinding. I have absolutely no interest in firing up NG+...
but that's probably on me. Still, tons of game to be had, and most of it's pretty fun until you decide to grind that wondrous RPG grind.

Really enjoyed this game. Tons of fun. Hilarious. Highly recommend.
That said, to the guy who made the final boss randomly one-hit KO you so that you have to restart and there's no save point before the fight so you have to re-run the dungeon all over again, to you sir, I hope that every chocolate chip cookie you put in your mouth instantly becomes oatmeal raisin.

Yakuza: Like a Dragon is a real gift for fans of the series and a perfect entry point for newcomers. The game features incredibly well-developed characters — each with their own story, personality, and charisma — that you can’t help but follow from start to finish. The story keeps you hooked, constantly surprising you with twists and making you genuinely care about the heroes.

The new turn-based combat system turned out to be a brilliant choice: it feels fresh for the series while offering plenty of room for tactics, all without losing the drive and energy that fans love. And the new main protagonist, Ichiban Kasuga, is in no way inferior to the legendary leads of previous games — he’s charming in his own unique way, funny, yet deeply human and capable of touching your heart.

This is a game that perfectly combines drama, humor, great mechanics, and unforgettable characters. I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone who wants to dive into the vibrant and emotional world of the Yakuza series.

On top of that, the game is perfectly optimized for the Steam Deck, running smoothly and looking fantastic on the handheld — making it easy to enjoy this epic adventure anywhere.

This game was nice all, tons of explorations and activities to do, I honestly really enjoyed playing this game.
BUT, after the final boss fight the game decided to fucking froze for no reason and now I have to go not only the millenium tower again but also that fuckass underground dungeon that took me ages to complete. Honestly, fuck yall who made this game and I'm sure that I'm not the only one who had this issue.

This was my first yakuza game to play ever, and oh boy I loved it. I wasn´t sure what I was getting into, but by the end of the game I was crying like a baby over the tragic story of Ichi.

The characters where really fun, and the gameplay was really cool! So over the top haha

As someone who loves JRPGs, I really love turn based battles and Yakuza: Like a Dragon is a step up from the likes of Final Fantasy and Dragon Quest.

It has its lighthearted and serious moments which I really enjoy especially Ichiban's character development towards his other friends and people around him.

If you can't go to Japan, you can always feel free to explore the overworld of this game! It will make you enjoy and appreciate the sights of Japan.
I was invested after the first chapter and make 1 million Yen from collecting cans and pawning a regal bag. This game is a treasure and pleasure and i am going to enjoy beating it.
Its a Yakuza, so expect a lot of dialogues and shit. That being said great characters, great story and a almost genial job system.

A great entry into the Yakuza series and one of the best JRPGs out there. Great story, great character design, likable main characters, fun combat system, good amount of content, great music. Fortunately a sequel has been confirmed already!
Was hesitant at first, but love it! If you're worried about lore, you can go into this with little to not lore knowledge. As a series fan i consider this as one of the top 5.

Coming to Yakuza was the best decision of my life, all Yakuza games have a special charm, although Yakuza:Like a Dragon has a Jrpg gameplay, different from previous versions, but not inferior to other games. The game's fast tempo and satirical storytelling make the it extremely entertaining, not boring like many other turn-based games.

This was my first LaD game and it got me hooked! 
The story was outstanding, emotional, funny at times but also serious as well. I went through the 5 stages of grief playing this game

I have never properly played a turn based combat game before and this was insanely fun. Getting the timing right on guarding, the skills are hilarious, the essences (ultimates I guess they would be considered as) cutscenes were so creative. And of course in typical Yakuza fashion, being able to use items on the side of the road like bikes, traffic cones, sign boards etc was so fun. Nothing better than wiping out a gang of losers with a giant bicycle

I was genuinely surprised how much I actually enjoyed playing this game and was shocked at how invested in the story I became to be. Including the substories! There's so many amazing substories/quests in this game that I will remember for a long time (especially Nancy, anddd the clementine ;-;)
Ichiban's character is so full of love, kindness, childlike wonder and hope. He is by far one of my favourite protagonists of all time.

I love the jobs you can change too, you can really find what combat style you like playing the most and work around your parties composition. I love the minigames and the dungeon runs too. 

100000000/10.
so much content and chapters to invest in and unlock i give it a solid score 8.7

Game is slightly different in terms of battle style and closer to Persona series. It makes it unique in comparison with other title and it still includes even bigger amount of gameplay posssibilities.

I'd never played a yakuza game before so I picked this up and it hooked me immediately. It's such a great time in every aspect and I'll definitely be getting the other games in the yakuza series afterwards!
I've sunk a ton of time into this series and in my opinion this is the best title yet. Fantastic story, fun combat, and an absurd amount of side content to play through.

This game fulfills my wildest and most unrealistic fantasies such as going to the movies with friends, eating at restaurants with friends, singing karaoke with friends, and crawling around in the sewer with friends.

This game is perfect in every single way. I honestly hate turn-based RPGS with a passion, and even though I have never played another yakuza game(gonna work my way through them eventually) this game has so much heart, passion, and comedy behind it I love it.

A story on par with Zero, and only a few things that feel out of place or plain bad. (Mirror Face)
With this being RGG's first RPG, I did play with Legend's Remix (as I do most of the Yakuza games) and I can say that it was a fantastic RPG for their first time. The transition between the beat'em ups to this RPG feels jarring at first, but I did come around to love the characters and the stories. There's already a lot introduced that really wraps Ichiban around his friends with the bonds, and we're well rewarded for them too. There's a weird difficulty spike once you depart from Yokohama, and it caught me by surprise due to the boss(es) there. But, I suppose they did provide a dungeon to grind in before, so I guess that's both on me and RGG.

Still, I solid RPG that I thoroughly recommend.
I will keep it simple. I like this game, even though I am happy they did not do JRPGs for the next installments. I prefer my Ryo ga gotoko games to be brawlers :)
I cried over middle-aged people finding friendship and redemption in the gutters of a yakuza infested town. 10/10, Kasuga is the greatest homie.

Probably one of the best jrpgs I played in recent time.

The characters are fun and well written, the story is engaging, the side content is enjoyable, the classes all feel unique and different and it still keeps the fun, whacky yet still serious in certain moments yakuza feel.

100% a recommend for every Yakuza fan... and actually also for all that just enjoy a unique and well paced jrpg set in our modern times.

I have ignored it for God knows how many since I am not a fan of Yakuza, but when I cleared my backlog, I gave this game a chance and I am so glad I did. Bought this on sale with infinite wealth but this is a game I have no problems paying with the full price if I had known any better.

For whatever reason the long cutscenes and dialogues bored me. It goes on & on & on. I could not even watch half of it without getting distracted to do something else. It just doesn't keep you engaged. Never had any issue like this in the other Yakuza games.

A refreshing change of pace from the usual beat 'em up genre. The main story has more comedy sprinkled into it compared to the old games, so if you liked the separation of the jokes from the main story in the old games this might be a negative for you. Its very well worth playing this though, veteran to the series or not.

Main guy is a middle aged chad boomer that doesn't know how to use a smart phone, very likeable same with the rest of the cast. Funny humor, lots of content. Combat system is not too difficult and is easy going for filthy casuals like myself.

Much anticipated and if you were an ex-yakuza player, this is the new addition to the collection for you! The scenery uses real life locations from Japanese locations such as Isezakicho, Kabukicho and Dotonbori and it adds another level of detail which has never been seen in any Yakuza game made before it. This is a major leap in the world of Yakuza and it adds more control in every aspect. Most of the buildings can be entered instead of being there as a placeholder and with this, it provides more realism during the game.

probably one of the best JRPGs I've ever played. Not even kidding. The humor and and tone are awesome.
the gameplay rocks and it is in general a very great game.

Probably the funnest RPG I've played in a long time. It didn't feel overly grindy and there were fun side missions and jokes spread all around. Enjoyable characters and fun banter between them, great take on spells using modern-day objects and scenarios. Turn off English VA to save your ears.

The Ryu Ga Gotoku team has done it again with this one. It's got a little something for everyone. Melodrama, action, comedy, and a compelling story, as per usual. I'd recommend this to just about anyone, with the one caveat being that the last third of the game sees some intense difficulty spikes and you will need to grind to get some things done. That's the only thing I can truly complain about though.

Fantastic storytelling, as expected from the franchise.
Its not just another action packed game, it draws you into the rich,deep story as it unfolds and you won't feel like skipping past.
The attack skills on some of the characters are really hilarious but they hit hard.
Plenty of side quests and side stories within the main game itself. Enjoyed the "slice of life" conversations/banter between the MC and his friends when they eat at certain places or walk past places of interest.

You may hit a wall when you need to enter the Omi alliance building and you may have to grind for a few levels in the sotenbori arena.
But overall its a really great game you won't regret playing.

This is the best price to value games out there in the RGG catalogue, go cop this on sale. It's basically a dragged out version of the usual Yakuza games cus it's a turn based rpg, but it's absolutely worth it to sink your time into, so much to experiment and side contents to do, they nailed the genre shift well. It's got pacing issues in the end cus of the difficulty spikes to the point that i'd say it's a slog. it's a thing especially in JRPGs and i don't normalize it myself, but even after allat i still can say that this game is really enjoyable.
Funny game that jump scares you with good writing, likable characters, and insane plot twists immediately after playing 10 minutes karaoke. One of the best games of all time.
The only Yakuza game which gave me the same feelings when I first started the Yakuza series (Yakuza 0). The gameplay can go duck itself, but makes sense story wise.

A great entry point into the series for beginners, but also a nostalgic trip through the series for veterans - Yakuza: Like a Dragon provides a fresh take on the series with combat that feels like a mixture of Dragon Quest and Persona with the chaos you'd expect from a Yakuza game, a huge plethora of sidestories and world content that makes the game world feel really lived in, and the narrative has a fresh, yet familiar feeling to it with protagonist Ichiban Kasuga being more of a charismatic leader, than Kazuma Kiryu's more stoic nature, with the differences represented through every aspect of the game.

The gear and upgrade system is in-depth and paced, though to complete the game's post-story endgame content you will need to max out everything you can, as the encounters are more than willing to leave you on your ass again and again.

Overall, yeah, just get it for the Karaoke tbh, if you need any other reason to play this game. Maybe get the middle tier version of the game too, as some of the DLC isn't as worth it.

fun turn-based combat, good-to-great story beats, a lot of well-implemented systems & minigames, and a good feeling of rpg-style progression in the sense you start pretty weak but can end up pretty op if you've taken the time to level up characters and gear. this game also knows when to be incredibly silly and it knows when to take things more seriously. it's all over the place, yet somehow manages to gel together into something truly special. i'm sure it's not for *everyone* - but i do think most people would garner some level of enjoyment out of it.
story is good but gameplay is awful, i love turn based games but some of the bosses are just straight bs

Never before have I hated a game as much as Yakuza 7, it is the only game I’ve ever put down out of frustration with how poorly designed it is. Balancing is a mess, the level spike in Chapter 12 is insulting, and the combat is so boring and repetitive you don’t even want to grind to keep going. I have no issues with jrpgs, but Yakuza 7 is a bad jrpg. After hours of grinding I had no interest anymore in finishing the game normally so i downloaded cheats and just finished the story. Yakuza 7 in its current form should have stayed as what it began as, an April Fools joke. I was sick of grinding to make one number become a different one just so I could continue a story I no longer care about because there is a massive brick wall in the middle of it. I am sick of Yakuza 7.
Absolutely amazing, I am so thankful to have played this game. Bought the entire series regardless of similar gameplay, if the writing is the same I will love them.

First Yakuza game I've ever played, Had an absolute blast. Ichi and his friends are so memorable and charming and the game was such a crazy good experience from start to finish. The only flaw I have is that Kasuga doesn't exist in real life.
